report:
## Report

Your skepticism is well-founded — the claim that influenza vaccination *causes* Alzheimer's disease is not supported by scientific evidence, and the research actually points the opposite direction.

Multiple large observational studies have found flu vaccination is associated with a **reduced**, not increased, risk of Alzheimer's disease. A claims-based cohort study of older U.S. adults using propensity-score matching found flu vaccination associated with roughly a 40% lower risk of developing Alzheimer's over four years, an effect that grew stronger with repeated annual vaccination (https://neurosciencenews.com/flu-vaccination-alzheimers-20909/). This builds on earlier findings in veterans and patients with heart failure showing similar protective associations (https://medicalxpress.com/news/2016-05-flu-vaccination-dementia-patients-heart.html). Data presented at the Alzheimer's Association International Conference similarly linked flu and pneumonia vaccination to lower dementia incidence (https://aaic.alz.org/releases_2020/vaccines-dementia-risk.asp).

It's important to note these are observational, propensity-matched studies rather than randomized controlled trials, so they show association, not definitive proof of causation—but they point toward protection, not harm.

Separately, the false idea that vaccines (including flu and COVID-19 shots) *cause* Alzheimer's or dementia has circulated as misinformation, often tied to a widely debunked, non-peer-reviewed paper about mRNA vaccines. Fact-checkers at Reuters and PolitiFact reviewed these claims and found no credible scientific basis for vaccines causing Alzheimer's or related neurodegenerative disease (https://www.reuters.com/article/fact-check/no-evidence-that-pfizers-covid-19-vaccine-causes-alzheimers-disease-idUSL1N2MZ382/; https://www.politifact.com/factchecks/2021/feb/26/j-bart-classen/coronavirus-vaccine-doesnt-cause-alzheimers-als/).

**Conclusion:** The claim is false. Current evidence suggests influenza vaccination is associated with lower, not higher, Alzheimer's risk, while claims of vaccines causing the disease stem from debunked misinformation.
